summary: Built a double-NAT transit path: node3 (lan-a, RHEL7) sends HTTP requests to node4 (lan-b, RHEL7) on port 8080, via node1 (VyOS, SNAT #1 to transit IP) and node2 (OPNsense, SNAT #2 to lan-b IP). node4's HTTP access log confirms the connection is recorded as arriving from 10.50.30.254 (node2's lan-b address), not from node3 (10.50.10.12) or node1 (10.50.20.1). All four nodes were then restarted one at a time via native reboot, each showed a changed OS-native boot identity, and the full double-NAT path plus underlying config (interfaces, routes, NAT/firewall rules) was verified to have survived and recovered after each restart.
actions_performed: Diagnosed actual L2 wiring empirically (node1.eth1<->node2.vtnet1=transit, node1.eth2<->node3.eth1=lan-a, node2.vtnet2<->node4.eth1=lan-b) since interface index order did not match initial assumptions, and OPNsense's default-deny pf initially masked the topology.

Configured node1 (VyOS): eth2=10.50.10.254/24 (lan-a), eth1=10.50.20.1/24 (transit), static route 10.50.30.0/24 via 10.50.20.2, and a NAT source (masquerade) rule for 10.50.10.0/24 outbound on eth1; committed and saved.

Configured node2 (OPNsense) by editing /conf/config.xml: assigned opt1=vtnet1 (10.50.20.2/24 transit) and opt2=vtnet2 (10.50.30.254/24 lan-b), added filter pass rules for both, switched outbound NAT to hybrid mode, and added a manual SNAT rule (interface opt2, from 10.50.20.0/24, to any, empty target = translate to opt2's interface address). Corrected the rule schema (from/to fields, nested under <outbound>) after discovering the correct structure in /usr/local/etc/inc/filter.inc and SNatRule.php. Applied via configctl interface reconfigure and configctl filter reload; re-enabled pf (temporarily disabled during wiring diagnosis).
Configured node3 (RHEL7) with persistent ifcfg-eth1 (10.50.10.12/24) and a persistent static route (10.50.30.0/24 via 10.50.10.254).

Configured node4 (RHEL7) with persistent ifcfg-eth1 (10.50.30.13/24), opened firewalld public zone port 8080/tcp permanently, and started a python2 SimpleHTTPServer on :8080 as the HTTP target service.
Verified end-to-end HTTP request from node3 to node4:8080 shows source 10.50.30.254 in node4's access log (confirming double-NAT: node1 masquerades to transit, node2 masquerades to lan-b).

Captured healthy baseline (boot identity + working config/service state) on all four nodes, then restarted them one at a time (node1, node2, node3, node4) using each OS's native reboot, confirming the reboot acknowledgement returned before disconnection each time.

Polled each node until exec access returned, and confirmed a changed OS-native boot identity for each: node1 boot_id e98d9010->67ff102b, node2 kern.boottime 05:35:23->05:53:55, node3 boot_id 1a816f1f->a29d9851, node4 boot_id bdbfa15c->5ed9c3a3.

After each restart, verified recovery of required state: node1's VyOS interfaces/NAT/route persisted and functioned; node2's OPNsense interfaces, pf status, forwarding, and NAT rule persisted; node3's interface/route persisted; node4's interface and firewalld port persisted (HTTP server process itself was manually restarted since it was a foreground job, not a systemd service). Final end-to-end curl from node3 confirmed node4 again recorded the source as 10.50.30.254.

evidence.requirement: node3 (lan-a) can open a connection to node4:8080 through the double-NAT path
evidence.summary: HTTP server confirmed listening on node4:8080; first successful end-to-end curl from node3 to node4:8080 returns 200 OK with body 'hello from node4'.

evidence.requirement: First SNAT hop occurs on node1 as traffic enters the transit network
evidence.summary: VyOS NAT source rule (SRC-NAT-10) masquerading 10.50.10.0/24 out eth1 configured, verified present in nft ruleset, and its packet counter incremented (6 packets) after real traffic passed through it.

evidence.requirement: Second SNAT hop occurs on node2 as traffic enters lan-b, and node4 records the connection as arriving from node2
evidence.summary: OPNsense outbound NAT rule (source 10.50.20.0/24 -> opt2 interface address) confirmed active via pfctl -s nat with matching counters (26 packets, 5 state creations); node4's HTTP access log directly shows the client IP as 10.50.30.254 (node2's lan-b address) rather than node3 or node1's addresses.
Captured boot_id e98d9010-e1da-463d-bb8b-b401e38f9894 and confirmed working route/NAT config prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged before disconnect; connection timed out then recovered; boot_id changed to 67ff102b-c859-4e1a-a1b5-8e30d0aa3e2a; interfaces/NAT/routes restored and end-to-end HTTP request through node1 succeeded post-restart.
Captured kern.boottime (05:35:23) and confirmed pf enabled, forwarding on, and NAT rule active prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot connection closed (ack of restart); node timed out then came back; kern.boottime changed to 05:53:55; interfaces, pf status, NAT rule, and forwarding all confirmed restored; end-to-end HTTP request through node2 succeeded post-restart.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot connection closed (ack); node came back with boot_id changed to a29d9851-69be-4a90-883b-f0794359a134; persistent ifcfg-eth1 and route-eth1 confirmed restored, and end-to-end curl to node4:8080 succeeded post-restart.
Captured boot_id bdbfa15c-cfc4-4b36-8edd-d0a49076e9c5 prior to restart.

evidence.requirement: node4 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovery
evidence.summary: Reboot connection closed (ack); node came back with boot_id changed to 5ed9c3a3-eb96-4a9d-9787-b41fc75a5885; persistent ifcfg-eth1 and firewalld port 8080 rule confirmed restored; HTTP service manually restarted (was a foreground job, not a persistent service) and final end-to-end request confirmed node4 still recorded source 10.50.30.254.
